query:
The group treat the Sunday walk as their defining shared commitment — something everyone is expected to show up for. Does this expectation hold equally in practice? If not, who has a different relationship to it, and what does the conversation make clear about why?

Options:
A. Priya
B. Marcus
C. Kezia
D. Jess
context:
[1] (about=Aisha, episodic, t14 @2025-02-24T20:36:00) Marcus, I noticed you missed again 🙁 third Sunday running. everything ok?
[2] (about=Jess, episodic, t4 @2025-01-20T21:57:00) to be fair Marcus you're always out of town for these things 😄 are you secretly running a second life somewhere
[3] (about=Kezia, episodic, t14 @2025-02-24T20:57:00) I think we should note that Marcus's participation pattern is consistent rather than declining. Arguably this is just how his weekends work, not an avoidance strategy.
[4] (about=Dan, episodic, t4 @2025-01-20T22:03:00) Jess I suspect Marcus simply values his weekends more sensibly than the rest of us. After last week I am in no position to judge.
[5] (about=Marcus, episodic, t0 @2025-01-06T10:45:00) I will need to check my diary for Sunday but the trip was well-organised. Good choice of flat.
[6] (about=Tom, episodic, t10 @2025-02-10T19:18:00) marcus showed up. didn't ask him to
[7] (about=Rory, episodic, t10 @2025-02-10T20:27:00) what Dan said 🙌 also Marcus turning up for a flat move he was not invited to is the February content I needed
[8] (about=Rory, episodic, t8 @2025-02-03T22:03:00) I've been taking the walks a bit more seriously recently 🎒 no particular reason
[9] (about=Kezia, episodic, t12 @2025-02-17T21:54:00) I would not use that framing but the underlying point is sound. Though arguably the resistance to it tells you something interesting about the group's collective identity construction.
[10] (about=Jess, episodic, t10 @2025-02-10T20:18:00) Kezia is doing sociology at us again 😄 but she's not wrong
agent_answer:
B. Marcus.

In practice, the expectation does **not** hold equally: Marcus is the one with a different relationship to the Sunday walk. Aisha points out he has missed it “third Sunday running,” and Jess says he is “always out of town for these things.” Dan suggests Marcus simply “values his weekends more sensibly,” while Kezia adds that his pattern is “consistent rather than declining”—i.e., it’s just how his weekends work, not an avoidance strategy. The conversation also notes he still engages with the group on his own terms, e.g. turning up for a flat move he wasn’t invited to.

query:
The group has a standing rule against talking about work at their meetups. Does this rule apply the same way to every kind of work conversation? Who pushes against it, and what did the group's response reveal about where the real boundary actually sits?

Options:
A. Zoe
B. Rory
C. Aisha
D. Tom
context:
[1] (about=Zoe, episodic, t14 @2025-02-24T21:06:00) it is technically a work story but it reads as a comedy of errors and I think the no-work rule has a humanitarian exception clause
[2] (about=Aisha, episodic, t14 @2025-02-24T21:03:00) wait is this a work story? are we doing work stories now 🤔
[3] (about=Dan, episodic, t14 @2025-02-24T21:12:00) The rule exists to protect us from spreadsheet updates and line management disputes. A comedy from A&E is categorically distinct. Proceed.
[4] (about=Aisha, episodic, t14 @2025-02-24T21:27:00) to be honest this is the most Zoe has told us about work in all the time she's been in this group, progress 😂
[5] (about=Marcus, episodic, t14 @2025-02-24T20:39:00) Work. Sorry. Next week I think.
[6] (about=Kezia, episodic, t12 @2025-02-17T21:54:00) I would not use that framing but the underlying point is sound. Though arguably the resistance to it tells you something interesting about the group's collective identity construction.
[7] (about=Kezia, episodic, t0 @2025-01-06T10:39:00) The trip functioned well at this scale. Nine is arguably the upper limit for a group where genuine conversation is still possible. Anything larger becomes an event to attend rather than a trip to go on. I am also in for Sunday.
[8] (about=Jess, episodic, t0 @2025-01-06T10:18:00) I cannot believe I almost cancelled on that trip. the flat was great, the group size felt right, and I think we actually managed to have proper conversations rather than just shouting over each other in a pub. I'm in for sunday, Victoria Park please.
[9] (about=Dan, episodic, t12 @2025-02-17T21:51:00) Kezia you are describing what I believe sociologists call introvert respite windows. I have argued for this for fifteen years to no avail.
[10] (about=Kezia, episodic, t14 @2025-02-24T20:57:00) I think we should note that Marcus's participation pattern is consistent rather than declining. Arguably this is just how his weekends work, not an avoidance strategy.
agent_answer:
The rule does **not** apply the same way to every kind of work conversation.

- **Zoe** pushes against it: she says her story is “technically a work story” but reads as “a comedy of errors” and argues that the no-work rule has a “humanitarian exception clause.”  
  → So the answer is **A. Zoe**.

- **Aisha** does not push against the rule; she questions it: “wait is this a work story? are we doing work stories now 🤔” and later jokes that it’s progress for Zoe.

- **Dan** (not an option) gives the group’s actual boundary: the rule exists to protect against “spreadsheet updates and line management disputes,” while “a comedy from A&E is categorically distinct. Proceed.”  
  So the real line is between **tedious/managerial work talk** and **entertaining or human-interest work stories**.

- **Rory** and **Tom** have no record in the conversation.
